# Malformed `/https://` and `/http://` URL Root-Cause Analysis

Date: 2026-10-07
Scope: GSC "Page with redirect" exclusion, 4 example URLs:
`/https://alharrazlaw.com`, `/http://www.alharrazlaw.com`,
`/https://www.alharrazlaw.com`, `/http://alharrazlaw.com`

## Finding: not generated by this codebase

Every surface that builds a URL, href, canonical tag, hreflang alternate,
JSON-LD field, or sitemap entry was audited:

| Source | File | Pattern used | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Canonical / hreflang | `src/lib/seo.ts` (`buildMetadata`) | `/${locale}${path}`, always relative, resolved against `metadataBase` | clean |
| JSON-LD breadcrumbs/org | `src/lib/structured-data.ts` | `${siteConfig.siteUrl}${item.url}`, `item.url` always a relative `/...` path from each page's own breadcrumb array | clean |
| Sitemap | `src/app/(frontend)/sitemap.ts` | `${siteConfig.siteUrl}/${locale}${path}`, `path` sourced from `STATIC_PATHS` (hardcoded relative paths) and CMS `slug` fields (plain strings, no scheme) | clean |
| robots.txt | `src/app/robots.ts` | `${siteConfig.siteUrl}/sitemap.xml` | clean |
| IndexNow | `src/lib/indexnow.ts` | same pattern as sitemap | clean |
| Header / Footer / MobileCtaBar / Breadcrumbs / Button | all `src/components/layout/*`, `src/components/ui/Button.tsx`, `src/components/ui/Breadcrumbs.tsx` | every `href=` is either a relative `/${locale}/...` path, `tel:`, `mailto:`, or an external link built by `buildWhatsAppLink`/`buildTelLink` | clean |
| Language switcher | `src/components/layout/LanguageSwitch.tsx` | strips the locale prefix off the current pathname and re-prefixes with the target locale; cannot produce a nested full URL | clean |
| CMS data | `src/seed/data.ts` slugs, `src/payload-types.ts` slug fields | plain strings, no scheme, no dots (verified below) | clean |

**Live verification (2026-10-07):**
- `curl https://alharrazlaw.com/robots.txt` → one clean `Sitemap:` line, no malformed entries.
- `curl https://alharrazlaw.com/sitemap.xml` → 176 `<loc>` entries, zero contain a nested `http(s)://` inside another URL.
- Crawled all 176 sitemap URLs and grepped every returned HTML page for `href="/https` / `href="/http:` → **0 matches** (see Internal Link Crawl below).

Conclusion: no link, redirect, canonical, or metadata construction anywhere
in this Next.js application can produce a path of the form
`/https://alharrazlaw.com`. These URLs were not created by a link on our
own site.

## Most likely external origin

The 4 examples are exactly the 4 scheme/host variants of the domain itself
(`https`/`http` × apex/`www`) — not 4 unrelated URLs. That pattern is the
classic signature of the domain being **typed directly into a Search
Console or Bing Webmaster field that expects a relative sitemap path or
URL-inspection target and silently prepends the property's own domain**
(e.g. typing `https://alharrazlaw.com` into a "submit URL" or "add a
sitemap" box scoped to the `https://alharrazlaw.com` Domain property
produces exactly `https://alharrazlaw.com/https://alharrazlaw.com`). This
is consistent with the domain-migration work done earlier in this
engagement, where GSC/Bing property setup and sitemap submission were done
manually through the web UI. It can also be residual crawl history from
before this Next.js deployment existed on the domain. Neither explanation
involves our code.

## What DOES happen when one of these paths is requested (reproduced live)

```
curl -I "https://alharrazlaw.com/https://alharrazlaw.com"
→ HTTP/2 308, location: /https:/alharrazlaw.com
  (Vercel/Next.js's own platform-level normalization of a double slash
  "//" inside the path — not our proxy.ts)

curl -I "https://alharrazlaw.com/https:/alharrazlaw.com"
→ HTTP/2 404
```

This 308→404 chain is why GSC classifies these under "Page with redirect"
— it is a real, reproducible redirect, just not one our own code
intentionally issues at the first hop.

## Real bug found and fixed along the way

While reproducing this, `src/proxy.ts` was found to mis-handle the second
hop. Its `PUBLIC_FILE` regex (`/\.(.*)$/`, meant to let real static files
like `/logo.png` skip locale-redirect logic) matches **any dot anywhere in
the path**, not just a file extension on the last segment. Because
`/https:/alharrazlaw.com`'s last segment `alharrazlaw.com` contains a dot,
it was wrongly treated as a static-file request and fell through without
reaching our locale-redirect/not-found handling — a latent correctness bug
(it could theoretically mis-fire on a future real slug containing a dot,
though none currently do) that also made this specific garbage-path class
resolve through an accidental code path rather than a deliberate one.

**Fix applied** (`src/proxy.ts`):
1. `PUBLIC_FILE` narrowed to `/\.[^/]+$/` (extension on the final segment only).
2. Added an explicit guard: any path whose first segment looks like a URL
   scheme fragment (`/^\/https?:\//i`) now returns a direct `404` in one
   hop, instead of relying on the (now-fixed) regex to coincidentally
   produce the same result.

## Proof

- Typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) and lint (`eslint`) both clean after the fix.
- No test suite exists for `proxy.ts`; verified manually via the live
  `curl` reproductions above (before fix, documented in this file; after
  fix, to be re-verified once deployed — see validation plan).
- Full 176-URL sitemap crawl (see `CRAWL_RESULTS.md`) found zero
  `/https:`/`/http:`-prefixed internal links.

## What this means for the 4 flagged URLs

Because the source is external (not a link we emit), **there is nothing
further to "fix" in application code for these 4 specific URLs** beyond
the proxy.ts hardening above. They will fall out of GSC's "Page with
redirect" bucket on their own re-crawl (likely reclassified as 404 / Not
Found, which is the correct terminal state for a URL that never
corresponded to a real page). No redirect rule should be added that
"handles" them specially — adding one would just be redirecting them
without fixing a source, which the brief explicitly says not to do, and
there is no source on our side to fix.

**Recommendation for the human-side GSC/Bing error**: when manually
submitting a sitemap or URL in Search Console / Bing Webmaster Tools going
forward, enter the relative path only (`sitemap.xml`), not the full
`https://alharrazlaw.com/...` URL, since the Domain property UI already
prepends the domain.
